We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito-based authentication layer for a Lex chatbot web UI, supporting both authenticated and unauthenticated access, with IAM roles for either Lex V1 or Lex V2 depending on which bot is provided, and an optional policy to allow invoking a live chat API. The template should include a Cognito user pool with email as the username alias and auto-verified email, requiring given_name, family_name, email, and preferred_username as required attributes, a user pool client with no secret, and a Cognito identity pool that allows unauthenticated identities and is linked to the user pool. It must also create identity pool role attachments and separate IAM roles for authenticated and unauthenticated users, each with appropriate trust policies for Cognito and policies that grant either Lex V1 actions (like PostText and PostContent) or Lex V2 actions (like RecognizeText and RecognizeUtterance) based on a condition, plus a Polly synthesise speech permission for authenticated roles. The template should accept parameters for the identity pool name (default "identity pool"), the Lex V1 bot name (default "OrderFlowers") and optional Lex V2 bot ID and alias ID, a ForceCognitoLogin flag (default false) that, when true, denies unauthenticated Lex and API actions, and a ShouldEnableLiveChat flag (default false) that conditionally adds an execute-api invoke permission for a livechat endpoint. The deployment should choose Lex V1 if the bot name is provided and Lex V2 if the bot ID is provided, and the template should export the identity pool ID, user pool ID, and user pool client ID as outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain passengerlist.org, and provisions all necessary DNS record sets including TXT records for SPF and site verification, MX records for G Suite email with standard priority values, a DMARC TXT record on the _dmarc subdomain, A and AAAA alias records pointing the root domain and multiple subdomains (www, departures, join, athena, feed) to their respective CloudFront distributions using the standard CloudFront alias hosted zone ID, CNAME records for Zendesk mail routing, DKIM verification, and Squarespace domain verification, and CNAME records for AWS ACM certificate validation across several subdomains, using dynamically fetched or referenced values where those resources would be provisioned separately.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a complete authentication infrastructure for a customer support system using Amazon Cognito, with a user pool configured to use email as the username with auto-verification, two user groups named "admin" and "customer" where admin has higher precedence, a web application client using authorization code grant flow with a custom read scope and callback/logout URLs, a machine-to-machine client using client credentials grant with the same read scope, a resource server defining that scope, a Cognito domain for the hosted UI, a Lambda function that automatically adds new sign-ups to the customer group, and SSM parameters storing the client IDs, user pool ID, OAuth scope, discovery URL, token endpoint, authorize endpoint, and domain under the path /app/customersupport/agentcore/ for consumption by backend services.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the required IAM roles for SageMaker project templates, allowing each role's creation to be controlled independently via a parameter that defaults to "YES" except for the launch role and use role which default to "NO", and each role should be scoped to the /service-role/ path with a maximum session duration of one hour, with the launch role and use role having a deletion policy of Retain, and the template must output all eleven role ARNs, including the AmazonSageMakerServiceCatalogProductsExecutionRole attached to the AmazonSageMakerFullAccess managed policy, the AmazonSageMakerServiceCatalogProductsLaunchRole attached to the AmazonSageMakerAdmin-ServiceCatalogProductsServiceRolePolicy, the AmazonSageMakerServiceCatalogProductsUseRole attached to the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess managed policy plus an inline policy granting specific permissions across SageMaker, CloudFormation, CloudWatch, CodeBuild, CodeCommit, CodePipeline, EC2 (including network interface management for VPC-connected jobs), ECR, Events, Firehose, Glue, IAM, Lambda, Logs, S3, Step Functions, CodeStar Connections, KMS, and SSM, and the remaining service roles for CloudFormation, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, Events, API Gateway, Firehose, Glue, and Lambda each having their respective AWS-managed service role policies attached.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC spanning two availability zones with a CIDR block of 10.10.0.0/16 and DNS hostname resolution enabled. The template should provision two public subnets (10.10.0.0/24 and 10.10.1.0/24) and two private subnets (10.10.10.0/24 and 10.10.11.0/24), each in separate availability zones. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a complete AWS standby deployment for a cross-cloud disaster recovery blueprint where the primary cloud is OCI, including a VPC with a CIDR block of 10.82.0.0/16, a single private subnet using 10.82.10.0/24, an EC2 instance of type t3.micro dynamically fetching the latest Amazon Linux 2023 AMI that serves a simple static HTML page on HTTP port 80 to act as a health-check endpoint, and an Elastic IP associated to that instance for a stable failover endpoint; the instance must use a new IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy, have encrypted EBS volumes, enforce IMDSv2, and be placed in a security group that only allows HTTP and HTTPS ingress from the internal network range 10.0.0.0/8 and HTTPS egress to the same range; the VPC should have an Internet Gateway, a default route to it, and VPC Flow Logs enabled with encryption using a new customer-managed KMS key and a 30-day retention log group; all resources should be tagged appropriately for the DR standby role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route 53 hosted zone for the domain parameter prxu.org (with a trailing period) in the Production environment for use with Google Workspace email services, including apex TXT and MX records with a 300 second TTL for domain verification and email routing to Google's mail servers, plus alias records (A and AAAA) pointing to the respective CloudFront distributions for the dovetail-cdn, dovetail-cdn-staging, feeder CDN (f, f-staging, f.development), ad files CDN (a), and a development sandbox CDN (ryan-cdn) subdomains, along with legacy CNAME records pointing to the corresponding dovetail-cdn subdomains with a 3600 second TTL, CNAME records for the authenticated feed proxy subdomains (production and staging) with a 3600 second TTL, CNAME records for the dovetail router covering production and staging subdomains with a 30 second TTL, and all necessary ACM DNS validation CNAME records for certificates covering the various service and environment-specific subdomains.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a simple VPC setup for learning purposes, with an optional internet gateway, public subnet, route table, and security group controlled by boolean parameters, using a configurable naming prefix defaulting to "SimpleApp1", a VPC CIDR of 10.0.0.0/16, a public subnet CIDR of 10.0.1.0/24 in the first available availability zone in the region, and a security group that allows HTTP and HTTPS traffic from a specified source IP range defaulting to 0.0.0.0/0, with the only output being the VPC ID.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a landing zone hub VPC for multi-account spoke attachment, using an environment name prefix defaulting to "landing-zone", a VPC CIDR of 10.0.0.0/16, public subnets 10.0.1.0/24 and 10.0.2.0/24, private subnets 10.0.10.0/24 and 10.0.11.0/24 across two AZs, NAT gateways in each public subnet, public and private route tables, and a Transit Gateway with a private ASN of 64512 and DNS and VPN ECMP support enabled, along with private routes that send 10.0.0.0/8 traffic toward the Transit Gateway for spoke connectivity. Please include the necessary IAM roles, security groups, and standard resource tagging as best practices, and make the core infrastructure reusable by exporting key resource IDs such as the VPC, subnets, and Transit Gateway.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained Student Services agent infrastructure for an educational platform using AWS Bedrock AgentCore, where each agent or microservice domain gets its own Cognito user pool for OAuth2 client credentials authentication and its own IAM execution role with least-privilege permissions specific to its function. The template should include a shared base IAM managed policy granting Bedrock model invocation, CloudWatch logging and metrics under the bedrock-agentcore namespace, X-Ray tracing, and Systems Manager parameter access for the student-services path, and attach this base policy to every execution role. For the StudentServicesAgent orchestrator, create only the execution role without a Cognito pool because its inbound authentication is IAM-based. For the StudentServicesGateway, create a Cognito user pool, a custom domain using the account ID, a resource server with an access scope, and a confidential app client using client_credentials flow, but no execution role. For the CourseRegistration domain, create an execution role that includes the base policy plus full DynamoDB access, along with self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. For the CourseCatalog domain, create an execution role with the base policy plus an inline policy allowing bedrock:Retrieve on any knowledge base, plus self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. For the CourseReview domain, create an execution role with the base policy plus DynamoDB read-only access, plus self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. For the LoanApplication domain, create an execution role with the base policy plus an inline policy allowing sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint on any SageMaker endpoint, plus self-contained Cognito user pool, domain, resource server with access scope, and app client with client_credentials flow. All Cognito user pools should have relaxed password policies, auto-verify email, and require email as a schema attribute. All execution roles should assume trust by the bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com service with source account and source ARN conditions. The stack should export each execution role ARN, each user pool ID, each OIDC discovery URL, each app client ID, each token endpoint constructed from the custom domain pattern, and each OAuth scope for downstream cross-stack consumption.

We need a CloudFormation template that implements the full set of CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark section 3 log-based monitoring controls. It should create a CloudWatch Logs log group that will receive CloudTrail management events, along with a KMS customer managed key and an SNS topic (encrypted with that key) to receive alarm notifications. On top of that log group, create CloudWatch Logs metric filters, matching CloudWatch alarms, and companion Logs Insights query definitions covering each of the following conditions: unauthorized API call attempts, console sign-in without MFA, use of the root account, IAM policy changes, CloudTrail configuration changes, console login failures, disabling or scheduling deletion of customer managed KMS keys, S3 bucket policy changes, AWS Config configuration changes, security group changes, network ACL changes, network gateway changes, route table changes, and VPC changes. Each alarm should trigger when the corresponding event count reaches or exceeds a threshold of one within a five minute period (except the KMS key alarm, which should use a one minute period), treat missing data as not breaching, and publish its notification to the SNS topic created by the template.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route53 hosted zone for theworld.org with a parameterized domain name and comprehensive DNS record sets for a production and staging multi-environment web infrastructure. Include TXT records for email authentication such as SPF records, domain verification codes, and DMARC policies; MX records for email routing to Microsoft Office 365 and Google Workspace; and CNAME records for mail service providers including ZenDesk, Campaign Monitor, and other integrations. Configure alias records for the primary domain and environment-prefixed variants (prod, stag) to route traffic to a shared CloudFront distribution and various Application Load Balancers, covering multiple endpoint types such as frontend services, WordPress backends, administrative interfaces, APIs, feed services, project pages, and file repositories. Include DKIM records for email authentication and AWS Certificate Manager validation records for SSL certificate provisioning across the domain hierarchy.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a fully automated Security Hub deployment across our entire AWS Organization, leveraging AWS Control Tower. The solution should automatically enable Security Hub in the designated audit account as the delegated administrator, then enable Security Hub in the log archive account and any future accounts created via Control Tower, adding them as members. It must use EventBridge rules that react to the Control Tower lifecycle events indicating a new account was successfully provisioned and that the landing zone setup or update has finished, invoking SSM automation documents that handle the cross-account enablement, member invitation, and acceptance workflows. The automation should read the audit and log archive account IDs from configuration values stored under the "/superwerker/" path in Parameter Store, and should perform cross-account actions by assuming the cross-account administration role that AWS Control Tower automatically provisions in every account it manages, named "AWSControlTowerExecution". The template should define all required IAM roles, SSM documents, and EventBridge rules to make the process fully event-driven and self-service.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of shared IAM roles and supporting resources for use across multiple EKS deployments, with an optional environment alias and hash for naming, an optional PermissionsBoundary parameter (commented out but load-bearing for environments that require it), and an S3 bucket name parameter that scopes the bastion role's S3 GetObject access to only that bucket. The template should enable GuardDuty in the region with a finding publishing frequency of fifteen minutes, then create the following IAM roles: a Lambda execution role with read-only access for resource discovery, a Lambda role for getting the caller identity and accessing CloudFormation and CloudTrail logs, a role for describing EKS node groups, a CloudFormation execution role with a maximum session duration of 8400 seconds and broad permissions to manage EKS, Secrets Manager, KMS, S3, EC2, Lambda, and logging, a logging delivery role for CloudFormation registry logs, a role for CodeBuild and EKS service integration with permissions for ECR, S3, and EKS, a role for CloudFormation extension hooks with permissions for Secrets Manager, KMS, EKS, S3, STS, IAM, EC2, Lambda, logs, CloudWatch, and SSM, and a bastion instance role with access to the specified S3 bucket, ECR, EC2, EKS, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, and CloudWatch logs. Additionally, the template should activate three CloudFormation resource types for Kubernetes (AWSQS-Kubernetes-Resource, AWSQS-Kubernetes-Helm, and AWSQS-EKS-Cluster) using the execution role for execution and the logging delivery role for logging, with each activation writing to a specific log group (e.g., cloudformation/registry/awsqs-kubernetes-resource, awsqs-kubernetes-helm-logs, and cloudformation/registry/awsqs-eks-cluster). All roles should be named with the environment alias prefix and be self-contained within the stack.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained ECS environment consisting of a VPC, an ECS cluster, and a private Application Load Balancer with a listener, along with a containerized ECS service that runs on that cluster, using an environment name to derive resource identifiers. Deploy the specified Docker image with configurable CPU and memory resources, and configure the service to route traffic through the private load balancer with path-based routing and priority settings. Include automatic scaling policies triggered by CloudWatch alarms: scale the service up when CPU utilization exceeds 70 percent and scale it down when CPU falls below 20 percent, maintaining a running task count between 2 and 10 tasks with deployment health settings at 75 percent minimum healthy and 200 percent maximum.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive SQS infrastructure for testing purposes with a FIFO queue without a dead letter queue, a FIFO queue with a dead letter queue, its DLQ, a standard queue with a DLQ using a redrive policy with a maximum receive count of 5, that DLQ, a separate FIFO DLQ, and a KMS key to encrypt all queues, along with numerous CloudWatch alarms that monitor the standard queue's number of messages sent as a sum with a threshold of 1 breaching on missing data, the FIFO queue with DLQ's average number of messages sent using an anomaly detection band, the maximum sent message size on both the standard and the separate FIFO queue with a threshold of 183500 bytes, the sum of visible messages on both DLQs alerting when greater than zero, the maximum age of the oldest message on the standard and separate FIFO queue with a threshold of 15 and treating missing data, the maximum number of messages not visible on the standard and separate FIFO queue with respective thresholds of 108000 and 18000, the maximum age of the oldest message on the standard DLQ with a threshold of 90, and a synthetic always-OK alarm that evaluates to not breaching on missing data, with all alarms having actions disabled.

We need a CloudFormation template that builds the private networking infrastructure required to support a private Red Hat OpenShift on AWS (ROSA) cluster using AWS PrivateLink. It should create a private ROSA VPC (default CIDR 10.1.0.0/16) with one or three subnets depending on a selectable number of availability zones parameter, each subnet CIDR configurable via its own parameter, and a separate egress VPC (default CIDR 10.0.0.0/16) containing one public subnet and one private subnet with their own configurable CIDRs. The egress VPC's public subnet should host an internet gateway and a NAT gateway with its own Elastic IP, and a Transit Gateway (with default route table association and propagation disabled) should be created with its own route table, attached to both VPCs, and configured with routes so that the ROSA VPC's private subnets can reach the internet through the egress VPC's NAT gateway while return traffic and inter-VPC traffic route correctly through the Transit Gateway. Include parameters to optionally create the Elastic Load Balancing service-linked role and to optionally enable VPC Flow Logs, delivered to CloudWatch Logs and encrypted with a customer managed KMS key through an IAM role granting the flow logs service permission to write to the log group, for both VPCs. Output the key resource identifiers, including both VPC IDs, subnet IDs, the Transit Gateway ID, and the NAT gateway and internet gateway IDs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of prerequisite resources and nine distinct AWS Systems Manager Automation documents for automated remediation of specific PCI DSS controls, with all outputs exported for use by custom AWS Config conformance packs; the prerequisites include a CloudTrail CloudWatch Logs log group with a retention period of 1827 days, a KMS customer master key with key rotation enabled and a key policy granting full KMS access to the account root, an IAM role for the SSM automations to assume that is attached the IAMFullAccess and AdministratorAccess managed policies, and an IAM role for CloudTrail’s CloudWatch Logs integration with permissions to write log events, manage log groups and streams, and perform other necessary actions; the nine automation documents are: one that encrypts a given CloudTrail trail with a provided KMS key and also integrates it with CloudWatch Logs, one that enables key rotation for a specified KMS key, one that integrates a CloudTrail trail with CloudWatch Logs, one that updates the account’s IAM password policy to enforce a minimum password length of 14, require uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols, allow password change, set a hard expiry, a maximum password age of 90 days, and prevent reuse of the last 24 passwords, one that enables log file validation for a CloudTrail trail while also ensuring multi-region and CloudWatch integration, one that revokes all inbound and outbound rules on a given default security group, one that deletes a specified security group, one that releases an unused Elastic IP address given its allocation ID, and one that updates a CodeBuild project to remove any environment variables named AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

We need a CloudFormation template that sets up telemetry monitoring for Claude Desktop (CoWork) usage. It should create a CloudWatch Logs log group to receive CoWork events, along with a set of CloudWatch Logs metric filters that extract input tokens, output tokens, cache read tokens, cache creation tokens, estimated cost, and session turn counts from the log events, since CoWork emits its telemetry in two different event schemas depending on whether it runs in local agent mode or as Claude Code for Desktop, and filters should be created to capture metrics from both schemas into the same set of metric names, with dimensions or default values so filters that omit user or model attribution still populate a value of zero when unmatched. On top of these metrics, create a CloudWatch dashboard, with a configurable name, that displays total token usage, total cost, session turn counts, cache hit tokens, usage and cost trends over time, average cost per turn, per user breakdowns of token usage cost and session activity, active user counts, and a recent raw events log table, all scoped to a configurable metrics region that defaults to us-east-1. Output the direct console URL to the created dashboard.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained bootstrap environment for deploying AWS CDK applications, including an encrypted S3 bucket for file assets with versioning and HTTPS-only access, an immutable ECR repository with image scanning for container assets, a KMS key for bucket encryption with a customizable alias, IAM roles for file publishing, image publishing, account lookup, deployment actions, and CloudFormation execution with configurable trusted accounts and managed policy ARNs, an SSM parameter to track the bootstrap version, and support for custom asset bucket names or using an existing KMS key, all using a short qualifier string to uniquely identify the stack components in the same AWS account and region.

We need a CloudFormation template that builds a backend API for an NIH grants research assistant tool. It should create a Cognito user pool used to authenticate API callers, and a regional API Gateway REST API secured by a Cognito authorizer built on that user pool, exposing resources for searching grants, scraping web page context, generating prompt templates, checking template generation status, listing generated S3 artifacts, and querying the NIH Reporter grants API directly, each proxying to a backend Lambda function (or, for the NIH Reporter search, an outbound HTTP integration) and each also exposing a CORS-enabled OPTIONS method. Add a template generation endpoint that authenticates via the same Cognito authorizer but forwards requests directly into an SQS queue using an API Gateway service integration and a dedicated IAM role. The queue and its dead letter queue should both be encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, restricted to encrypted-in-transit access only, and configured with a redrive policy sending failed messages to the dead letter queue after five receive attempts. Deploy the API to a Dev stage, create an API key and a usage plan with a monthly request quota and throttle limits, and enable CloudWatch logging for the API Gateway account. Output the invoke URL of the deployed API and the created API key.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an Elastic Beanstalk environment supporting Blue-Green deployments, allowing the user to either create a new application and environment or reference existing ones for the blue deployment, with the ability to generate a temporary green environment for traffic routing during updates and then terminate it after routing traffic back to the blue environment; when creating new resources, the template should use a default application name and environment name, launch with a modern supported solution stack appropriate for the application, and deploy a sample application from a default S3 bucket, appending the current region to the bucket name only when using that default bucket.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS Service Catalog environment for a machine learning workshop, including two portfolios, one for an admin team and one for end users, with a set of products representing a VPC with private subnets and endpoints, IAM roles with KMS keys and S3 buckets, an AWS Data Exchange product, an infrastructure product, an application product, a SageMaker notebook instance, and a third-party ML model, each associated with its respective portfolio and constrained by a dedicated launch role that grants the necessary permissions for provisioning, and the template must also create the corresponding IAM roles for the Service Catalog admin lead end user and the standard end user, granting them appropriate read and describe permissions along with access to specific SSM parameters under the MLWorkshop path and S3 objects tagged for provisioning, and it must associate these roles as principals to the correct portfolios, and the template should accept two parameters, one for the root S3 URL pointing to the location of the nested CloudFormation templates with a default value of https://aws-service-catalog-reference-architectures.s3.amazonaws.com/blog_content/securing-third-party-data-and-ml-apps and one for an environment prefix that defaults to user-1, and it must output the switch role URLs for both the lead end user and the developer end user.

We need a CloudFormation template that provisions a single environment VPC with IPv4 and IPv6 dual stack support for either a staging or a production environment, selectable through a parameter, with the actual VPC and subnet CIDR ranges varying by environment as defined in the template. The VPC should contain three public subnets (two in the first availability zone for load balancer or presentation-tier use, one in an additional availability zone for compute or EC2 use) and two private subnets in the first availability zone for application and data tiers, all with matching IPv6 CIDR allocations derived from the VPC's auto-assigned IPv6 block, an internet gateway, an egress-only internet gateway for IPv6, and a public route table routing both IPv4 and IPv6 default traffic through the internet gateway. Include a parameter controlling whether to also deploy a NAT gateway, with its own Elastic IP, for the private subnets, since a NAT gateway may not be needed if a bastion host itself performs that role, and use two network ACLs: one for the public subnets allowing inbound HTTP, HTTPS, SSH, a bastion VPN port, and ephemeral return traffic (each for both IPv4 and IPv6) with open egress, and one for the private subnets allowing all inbound and outbound traffic. Also create an EC2 placement group for tightly coupled workloads and a DHCP options set assigning the environment's own domain name and the default Amazon-provided DNS servers to the VPC. Export the VPC ID, VPC CIDR, public and private subnet IDs, and the private route table ID as stack outputs so other stacks can reference this network.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a fully self-contained serverless movies API using Python 3.12, with a DynamoDB table using pay-per-request billing keyed on the title attribute, four Lambda functions for create, read, update, and delete operations against the table with 30-second timeouts and 128MB of memory, an API Gateway REST API with a regional endpoint configuration exposing POST, PUT, and DELETE on a /Movies resource and GET on a /Movies/{title} resource along with necessary CORS preflight support using MOCK integration, pre-created CloudWatch log groups with a 1-day retention for each function, and a single shared IAM role granting DynamoDB CRUD access to the table and the managed Lambda basic execution policy, with the API deployed under a stage named after the environment parameter which defaults to dev.

We need a CloudFormation template that provisions a SageMaker Studio user profile for an MLOps engineer persona along with an IAM execution role scoped specifically to that persona's responsibilities. The execution role should be assumable by the SageMaker service and should include policies allowing it to pass a per-user SageMaker execution role, manage SageMaker pipelines (create, start, stop, retry, and update pipeline executions, plus list and describe operations), manage model monitoring schedules and their underlying processing jobs, manage models and model package groups, view experiments, trials, and lineage information, run training, transform, processing, and hyperparameter tuning jobs, manage SageMaker endpoints, and use SageMaker Studio applications and shared or private spaces with an ownership restriction so a user can only manage apps and spaces they own. Accept optional parameters for an existing SageMaker Studio domain ID together with its associated security group IDs and subnet IDs; when the domain ID is not supplied, the template should instead create its own self-contained VPC, subnet, and public-internet-access SageMaker Studio domain, using the created execution role for its default user settings, and attach the new user profile to that domain instead. Output the ARN of the created user profile.

We need a CloudFormation template that sets up CloudWatch monitoring for a set of cross-language database encryption SDK performance benchmarks. It should create a CloudWatch Logs log group, with a configurable name defaulting to a benchmarks-specific name and a 30 day retention period, that receives structured JSON benchmark result events, and on top of it a comprehensive set of CloudWatch Logs metric filters covering five programming languages: Java, .NET, Python, Go, and Rust. For each language, create filters that extract a memory efficiency ratio and peak memory usage from memory test results, extract p50, p95, and p99 latency from throughput test results at a specific data size, and extract p50, p95, and p99 latency from concurrency test results, publishing each metric into a language-specific CloudWatch namespace with a dimension identifying the language. Output the log group name and the list of per-language metric namespaces created.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS AppSync GraphQL API named "TodoAPIwithJs" with API key authentication, backed by a DynamoDB table with a global secondary index on the owner attribute, and using JavaScript resolvers to support full CRUD operations (create, update, delete, get, list) as well as a query by owner index, along with real-time subscriptions for create, update, and delete events, all implemented as pipeline resolvers with individual JavaScript functions for each data operation.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive, self-contained set of IAM roles for the Data Master project, covering a data pipeline from ingestion through analytics. The template must accept two parameters: the ARN of an existing KMS key (used for raw data encryption) and the Target AWS Account ID (used to scope STS AssumeRole policies). Provision roles for DMS to write to Kinesis, EventBridge Pipes to forward data to Firehose, Lambda functions for processing and routing, Glue crawlers and ETL jobs, Lake Formation data lake access, Step Functions for orchestration, ECS Fargate tasks, EMR Serverless jobs, and AWS Managed Grafana for monitoring. Do not create a KMS key; instead, any roles requiring KMS encryption or decryption permissions (such as the Firehose access role, the processing controller function role, and the worker role) must grant access by referencing the provided KMS key parameter. The DMS VPC role must restrict its 'AssumeRole' policy statement using the provided Target Account ID parameter. Finally, ensure all roles are tagged with Project: DataMaster and Component: Roles, and export their ARNs utilizing a naming convention consisting of a 'dm-' prefix and a '-role-arn' suffix.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates composite CloudWatch alarms for monitoring the health of a cross-region failover application, targeting an existing Remittance API Gateway API, existing GetRemittances and CreateRemittance Lambda functions, and an existing dbcluster1-instance1 RDS instance, with composite alarms named API Gateway Health, Lambda Health, and RDS Health that each aggregate their underlying metric alarms with an OR-based alarm rule so that any single triggered condition trips the composite; for the API Gateway, alarm on 4XX errors averaging above 0 over a 300 second period, 5XX errors averaging above 1 over a 60 second period, and latency at or above 10000 milliseconds over a 300 second period, each evaluated over a single evaluation period with one datapoint to alarm and TreatMissingData set to notBreaching; for the Lambda functions, alarm when summed errors exceed 0 over a 60 second period and when summed invocations exceed 2 over a 60 second period, each with a single evaluation period, one datapoint to alarm, and TreatMissingData set to notBreaching (the invocations alarms feed into the Lambda Health composite, though the composite rule only references the errors and duration alarms), while the two duration alarms (average duration at or above 10000 milliseconds over a 900 second period, single evaluation period, one datapoint to alarm) have TreatMissingData set to missing; for the RDS instance, alarm on high CPU utilization averaging at or above 70 percent, database connections averaging at or above 100, deadlocks averaging at or above 10, network transmit and receive throughput each averaging at or above 10485760 bytes, queries averaging at or above 100, disk queue depth averaging at or above 50, and read and write latency each averaging at or above 0.1 seconds, each evaluated over a 300 second period with a single evaluation period and one datapoint to alarm, leaving TreatMissingData unset on every RDS alarm so CloudWatch's standard default treatment applies.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive monitoring and data extraction pipeline for an internal QuickSight admin console, using seven Glue jobs (five Python shell jobs with Python 3.9 and Glue version 3.0, and two ETL jobs with worker type G.1X and two workers using Glue version 5.0) to periodically collect asset access details, asset metadata, folder structure information, Q topic metadata, Q object access details, dataset properties, and data source properties, with each job having a specific name (etl_job_admin_suite_assets_access, etl_job_admin_suite_assets_metadata, etl_job_admin_suite_folder_assets, etl_job_admin_suite_q_metadata, etl_job_admin_suite_q_access, etl_job_admin_suite_ds_properties, and etl_job_admin_suite_datasource_properties), setting execution properties including MaxConcurrentRuns of 1, a timeout of 120 minutes, and for the ETL jobs max retries of 0, with default arguments passing the AWS region and account ID where appropriate, all scripts fetched dynamically from a predefined S3 script bucket path, storing all output in a newly created private S3 bucket named admin-suite-followed by the account ID with public access fully blocked and a DeletionPolicy of Retain, with each Glue job scheduled to run every 3 hours via its own scheduled Glue trigger, along with five CloudWatch metric streams using JSON output format capturing specific QuickSight metrics (IngestionRowCount, IngestionLatency, IngestionInvocationCount, and IngestionErrorCount for the first stream; VisualLoadTime, DashboardViewLoadTime, DashboardViewCount, and VisualLoadErrorCount for the second; SPICECapacityLimitInMB and SPICECapacityConsumedInMB for the third; QuickIndexDocumentCount and QuickIndexExtractedTextSize for the fourth; ActionInvocationError and ActionInvocationCount for the fifth), each feeding into a dedicated DirectPut Kinesis Firehose delivery stream that writes to the same S3 bucket with appropriate prefixes, and all of this managed by a single IAM role assumable by glue, cloudformation, firehose, and streams.metrics.cloudwatch services with permissions for QuickSight, Glue, S3, CloudWatch, Firehose, and IAM operations.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a fully self-contained serverless CRUD API for a "Kitten" service, using Amazon API Gateway with a DynamoDB table named "Kitten" that uses a partition key named "KittenId" of type string and is configured for on-demand billing, and the API must expose the following operations: a POST to the `/kitten` resource that auto-generates the KittenId from the request context and expects name and color fields in the request body, a GET on `/kitten` that scans all items, a GET on `/kitten/{id}` that retrieves a single item by its KittenId, a PUT on `/kitten/{id}` that expects name and color fields in the body to replace the item, and a DELETE on `/kitten/{id}` that removes the item, all with proper CORS support including an OPTIONS method on every resource that allows all origins and standard headers, and each method should return appropriate HTTP status codes for success, bad input, and internal server errors.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a standard Step Functions state machine with a single pass state that returns a result of 1, along with a version and an alias pointing to that version, and integrates the alias with various event-driven triggers including an API Gateway REST API with a GET method on a path that starts an execution, an EventBridge rule that matches terminated state changes, a scheduled EventBridge rule that runs every minute but is initially disabled, an EventBridge rule that responds to tag events from the AWS Tag service, and an EventBridge Scheduler schedule that runs every minute with flexible time windows disabled, with each trigger requiring its own IAM role with the necessary permissions to start executions on the alias.

We need a CloudFormation template that provisions the IAM identities and permission policies required by the Cluster API Provider AWS (CAPA) bootstrap process for a cluster that uses Amazon EKS. It should create three IAM roles assumable by EC2 (a control-plane role, a nodes role, and a controllers role that is also assumable by EKS pods), plus a separate EKS control plane role assumable by the EKS service with the AWS managed EKS cluster policy attached, and matching instance profiles for the control-plane, controllers, and nodes roles. Attach customer managed IAM policies granting the control plane role the EC2, Auto Scaling, load balancer, and KMS permissions needed to run the legacy in-tree AWS cloud provider, granting both the control plane and nodes roles the EC2, ECR, Secrets Manager, and SSM permissions needed for cluster nodes to register and pull images, granting the controllers and control-plane roles the broad EC2 networking, Auto Scaling, load balancer, launch template, and service-linked-role permissions needed by the Cluster API controllers to manage cluster infrastructure, and granting the controllers and control-plane roles EKS-specific permissions to create and manage EKS clusters, node groups, add-ons, Fargate profiles, and related IAM and KMS operations. Also create a standalone managed IAM policy intended for human users or groups that only need read only visibility into EKS clusters, node groups, and workloads through the console, without attaching it to any role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with managed NAT gateways for a general purpose networking foundation. It should provision a VPC with two public subnets and two private subnets spread across two availability zones appropriate for the deployment region, an internet gateway attached to the VPC, a NAT gateway, each with its own Elastic IP, in each public subnet, and route tables so the public subnets route through the internet gateway while each private subnet routes outbound traffic through its own availability zone's NAT gateway. Enable VPC flow logs delivered to a CloudWatch Logs log group, with a configurable retention period and traffic type to capture, through a dedicated IAM role granted permission to write to that log group. Add a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 attached to all route tables, and interface VPC endpoints for the ECR API and ECR Docker registry services in the private subnets with private DNS enabled, protected by a security group that only allows outbound HTTPS traffic within the VPC's CIDR range. Export the VPC ID, VPC CIDR, both availability zone names, all four subnet IDs, and the endpoint security group ID so other stacks can reference this network.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route 53 hosted zone for 'theworld.org' and populates it with a comprehensive set of DNS records to support a production media environment. The template must accept the domain name as a parameter (defaulting to 'theworld.org.') and apply standard organizational tags for the production environment. Configure a robust email security posture by creating a root TXT record combining SPF includes for Outlook, CreateSend, Google, Zendesk, and Sendergen, along with a DMARC record configured to reject failures and send reports to specified email addresses. Create MX records routing mail appropriately for the root domain, 'gsuite', 'o365', and 'bounce' subdomains. For web traffic, provision A and AAAA Alias records pointing to CloudFront distributions for various content subdomains (e.g., admin, api, projects, sitemap, feeds), and route the primary WordPress production and staging subdomains to their respective Application Load Balancers. Finally, include CNAME records for public feeds, Autodiscover endpoints, Zendesk mail routing, and AWS ACM validation records for the various subdomains, utilizing dummy values or parameters where appropriate for external endpoints and validation hashes.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC named with a "KerberosEMRonEKS" prefix to support a Microsoft AD infrastructure, using a 10.0.0.0/24 CIDR split into two public subnets (10.0.0.0/26 and 10.0.0.64/26) and two private subnets (10.0.0.128/26 and 10.0.0.192/26), each in a different AZ, with an Internet Gateway, two NAT Gateways each with an EIP, and the proper routing so that public subnets have default routes to the Internet Gateway and each private subnet has a default route to its respective NAT Gateway in the same AZ. The template should also include a KMS key for encrypting VPC flow logs with key rotation enabled, a VPC flow log sending all traffic to a CloudWatch log group with 30-day retention, and VPC interface endpoints in the private subnets for SSM, SSM Messages, EC2 Messages, and Secrets Manager, all using a shared security group that restricts inbound and outbound traffic to HTTPS from the VPC CIDR.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC spanning three availability zones with public and private subnets in each, suitable as the networking foundation for an Amazon Redshift deployment. The VPC's CIDR block should be derived from a numeric parameter representing the second octet of a 10.x.0.0/16 address range, so the overall network size can be adjusted at deploy time, with each of the three availability zones getting one /20 public subnet, with automatic public IP assignment enabled, and one /20 private subnet carved out of that range. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC, create one NAT gateway per availability zone, each with its own Elastic IP, placed in that zone's public subnet, and set up a single shared public route table routing to the internet gateway plus one private route table per availability zone routing outbound traffic through that zone's own NAT gateway. Create one network ACL for the public subnets and one for the private subnets, each allowing all inbound and outbound traffic, and associate them with their respective subnets. Add a gateway VPC endpoint for S3, with an open access policy, attached to all three private route tables. Output the VPC ID, CIDR block, all three availability zone names, all subnet and route table IDs grouped by tier and availability zone, and the S3 VPC endpoint ID.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained SageMaker Domain configured in VPC Only mode with a single test user profile, along with a dedicated IAM role that grants the user full permissions to manage SageMaker jobs, experiments, models, and Studio applications, including the ability to create, stop, describe, and list training, transform, processing, AutoML, and hyperparameter tuning jobs, manage experiment lineage and artifacts, create and manage model packages and groups, and handle Studio apps, spaces, and presigned domain URLs, with the role also having read-write access to a specific default S3 bucket for the domain and the ability to pass itself to SageMaker services; the template should accept parameters for the domain name, the test user name, the ARN of the default S3 bucket, the VPC ID, a comma-separated list of subnet IDs, and a comma-separated list of security group IDs, and it must output the domain ID, the execution role name, and a direct URL to the SageMaker Studio console for the new domain.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of about 19 saved CloudWatch Logs Insights queries for analyzing usage, performance, and cost metrics generated by a Claude Code application, with all queries scoped to the log group /aws/claude-code/metrics (exposed as a parameter defaulting to that value) and organized into logical groups covering real-time monitoring (token and request rate per user, current TPM/RPM averages, and rate-limit risk), user and session analytics (session-level usage, hourly activity timelines, and error/throttling detection), cost and attribution reporting broken down by user, model, and organization, and additional debugging and analysis queries covering model efficiency, cache hit/miss rates (overall, over time, and by session), peak usage windows, deep-dive lookups for a specific session, a field explorer for discovering available metric attributes, and a daily usage summary, so engineers and finance stakeholders can review these queries on demand from the Logs Insights console.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AppSync GraphQL API named "SuperCoolAPI" with AWS IAM authentication and full CloudWatch Logs request logging, a DynamoDB table named "Table1" with an "id" string primary key and on-demand billing, multiple DynamoDB data sources connected to the table using different approaches to table and region referencing, IAM roles and policies granting full read-write access to the DynamoDB table and its secondary indexes, and a GraphQL schema defining a Todo type with id and description fields, including a getTodo query and an addTodo mutation.

We need a CloudFormation template that provisions the IAM identities and permission policies required by the Cluster API Provider AWS (CAPA) bootstrap process for a cluster that uses Amazon EKS with managed node groups and Fargate support. It should create IAM roles assumable by EC2 for the control plane, controllers (also assumable by EKS pods), and nodes, along with matching instance profiles for those three roles, plus three additional service roles: an EKS control plane role assumable by the EKS service with the AWS managed EKS cluster policy attached, an EKS Fargate execution role assumable by the EKS Fargate pods service with the AWS managed Fargate pod execution policy attached, and an EKS managed node group role assumable by both EC2 and EKS with the AWS managed worker node, CNI, and container registry read only policies attached, in addition to attaching those same three worker node policies directly to the plain nodes role. Attach customer managed IAM policies granting the control plane role the EC2, Auto Scaling, load balancer, and KMS permissions needed to run the legacy in-tree AWS cloud provider, granting both the control plane and nodes roles the EC2, ECR, Secrets Manager, and SSM permissions needed for cluster nodes to register and pull images, granting the controllers and control-plane roles the broad EC2 networking, Auto Scaling, load balancer, launch template, and service-linked-role permissions needed by the Cluster API controllers to manage cluster infrastructure, and granting the controllers and control-plane roles EKS-specific permissions to create and manage EKS clusters, node groups, add-ons, Fargate profiles, and related IAM and KMS operations.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a configurable multi-tier VPC network that can be deployed with one, two, or three tiers (for example public, private, and restricted) spread across a selectable number of Availability Zones, up to three. The stack should let each tier be individually enabled and named, and expose a CIDR parameter for the VPC along with separate CIDR parameters for each tier's subnet in each Availability Zone. It should optionally create an Internet Gateway with routing for the first tier, and optionally create NAT Gateways for outbound access from the other tiers, with a choice between a single shared NAT Gateway or one NAT Gateway per Availability Zone. VPC Flow Logs should be enabled and delivered to a CloudWatch Logs group through a dedicated IAM role, and there should be an optional parameter to attach a permissions boundary to that role. Subnet IDs and the VPC ID should be exposed as stack outputs for use by other stacks.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a shared VPC to support EMR on EKS and a Celeborn shuffle service cluster, with two public subnets and two private subnets spread across two Availability Zones, each with its own CIDR block parameter. The stack should include an Internet Gateway for the public subnets and a NAT Gateway per Availability Zone for outbound access from the private subnets, along with the associated route tables and subnet associations. It should also create an S3 gateway endpoint reachable from all route tables, and interface VPC endpoints, protected by a dedicated security group that only allows HTTPS from the VPC's own CIDR range, for Systems Manager, EC2, CloudWatch Logs, CloudWatch Monitoring, STS, EMR, and KMS, so that instances in the private subnets can reach these AWS services without going through the NAT Gateway. Finally, it should enable VPC Flow Logs for all traffic, encrypted with a dedicated customer-managed KMS key that the stack creates itself, delivering to a CloudWatch Logs group through a dedicated IAM role. The VPC ID, VPC CIDR, and all subnet IDs should be exposed as stack outputs so other stacks can reference them.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC, with a parameterized identifier and CIDR block, that has both an IPv4 range and an Amazon-provided IPv6 range associated with it, spread across three Availability Zones. Include a parameter that lets the deployer choose whether to include public subnets at all; when enabled, the stack should create three public subnets, one per Availability Zone, each carved out of the VPC's own IPv4 and IPv6 ranges, an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC, and a single public route table with a default route to the internet, associated with all three public subnets. Regardless of that choice, the stack should always create three private subnets, again one per Availability Zone with both IPv4 and IPv6 ranges, and a single private route table associated with all of them, though it does not need a default route to the internet. Expose the VPC ID and the lists of public and private subnet IDs as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that provisions the full set of IAM identities and permissions required to bootstrap and operate the Cluster API Provider for AWS, so that a Kubernetes cluster's control plane, controller manager, and worker nodes can each assume a dedicated role with least-privilege access. Create separate IAM roles for the control plane, the controllers, the worker nodes, and a role dedicated to the EKS control plane, each with a matching instance profile where relevant, assumable by the EC2 service (and, for the controllers role, also by EKS Pods), and each carrying the AWS managed policies appropriate to its function, such as the managed EKS cluster, worker node, and CNI policies. Attach managed IAM policies to the control plane and worker node roles granting the EC2, Elastic Load Balancing, Auto Scaling, ECR, Secrets Manager, and Systems Manager permissions the AWS cloud provider integration needs to manage those resources on the cluster's behalf, and attach a broader managed policy to the controllers and control plane roles covering the EC2 networking, load balancing, auto scaling, EKS cluster and nodegroup management, and related service-linked role creation permissions the cluster API controllers require. Also create an IAM group and an IAM user representing a bootstrapper identity used to run cluster lifecycle operations, with the group granted the same controller-level managed policy.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC infrastructure for OpenSearch cross-region resilience, deployable in both regions, with a configurable environment name (default "production"), a VPC CIDR of 10.0.0.0/16, three private subnets (10.0.1.0/24, 10.0.2.0/24, 10.0.3.0/24) and three public subnets (10.0.101.0/24, 10.0.102.0/24, 10.0.103.0/24) each in separate Availability Zones, an Internet Gateway, and an optional NAT Gateway setup that can be either a single NAT Gateway (cost-effective) or one per AZ for high availability, with the default being single; the template should also enable VPC Flow Logs with a 7-day retention period sent to CloudWatch Logs, and export all subnet IDs, VPC ID, and NAT Gateway IDs as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a completely isolated private VPC for hosting an AI-powered customer support application with no direct internet access. The VPC should span multiple availability zones with three private subnets and include VPC endpoints for AWS services: Bedrock for AI inference, ECR for container image retrieval, CloudWatch Logs and Monitoring for observability, DynamoDB, RDS Data API, Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store, KMS, S3, and X-Ray. Enable VPC Flow Logs for all traffic encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation. Create a dedicated security group for each application component (Agent Runtime, MCP Runtime, and Lambda functions) that allows HTTPS-only egress to the VPC endpoints, with the components that need it also permitted to reach DynamoDB directly.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC, with a parameterized CIDR block and a name used to tag resources, intended to host an Amazon EKS cluster, spread across three Availability Zones. It should include three public subnets and three private subnets, each with its own CIDR parameter, an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC with a public route table routing to it, and a NAT Gateway with its own Elastic IP in each public subnet, providing outbound internet access for the corresponding private subnet through per-Availability-Zone private route tables. Tag the private subnets appropriately for internal load balancer discovery. The stack should also create a security group intended for the EKS control plane to communicate with worker nodes, and a second security group exposing several application ports, including HTTP, HTTPS, and a handful of custom TCP ports used by an ingress or service mesh gateway, to the internet. Expose the VPC ID, the security group IDs, and the list of all subnet IDs as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM execution role for a SageMaker HyperPod cluster integrated with an EKS cluster, where the template accepts parameters for a resource name prefix, an EKS cluster name, a VPC ID, a list of security group IDs, a list of private subnet IDs, an S3 bucket name for lifecycle scripts, and optional parameters for a RIG input S3 bucket, a RIG output S3 bucket, a flag to create RIG resources, and a flag to enable gated access, and the role must be named by appending "ExecRole" to the prefix, allow the SageMaker service principal to assume it, be attached to the AWS managed policy for SageMaker cluster instance roles, and include a custom inline policy that grants the EKS CNI plugin permissions for attaching network interfaces, describing instances, tags, network interfaces, instance types, and subnets, and creating tags on network interfaces, along with a second inline policy that grants broader ENI management actions such as assigning private IP addresses, creating, deleting, and modifying network interfaces and permissions, and detaching network interfaces, scoped to instances, network interfaces, and the specified VPC, plus read permissions for VPCs, DHCP options, and security groups, ECR actions for pulling container images, CloudWatch alarm describe permissions, the eks-auth:AssumeRoleForPodIdentity action scoped to the provided EKS cluster, and list and get object access to the lifecycle scripts S3 bucket, and the template must also conditionally create a RIG policy when the RIG flag is true and a RIG input bucket is provided, granting list and get object access to that bucket, allowing Lambda invocation for functions with names containing SageMaker or sagemaker, and when the gated access flag is true, additionally granting get object access to specific S3 access points and buckets and SQS message actions on queues containing SageMaker or sagemaker, and if a separate RIG output bucket is provided, granting full read, write, and delete object access to that bucket, and the template must also conditionally create additional policies for each provided private subnet and security group that grant the same ENI management actions scoped to those specific subnet and security group resources, and all resources must be tagged with a key indicating they are SageMaker HyperPod prerequisites with a value equal to the role name, and the stack should expose the role name and ARN as outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates three private subnets (10.24.24.0/24, 10.24.25.0/24, and 10.24.26.0/24) in us-east-1a, us-east-1b, and us-east-1c respectively. Each subnet requires its own route table with a default route pointing to a NAT gateway (provided via three specific NAT gateway parameters, one for each AZ), and each subnet must be associated with a provided network ACL parameter. The template must be fully self-contained, accepting the target VPC ID, the three NAT Gateway IDs, and the Network ACL ID as standard parameters instead of relying on cross-stack imports. Additionally, provision an S3 VPC endpoint attached to all three route tables with a full-access policy. Finally, export a comma-separated list of the private subnet IDs, the route table IDs, and the subnet group CIDR (10.24.24.0/21) using export names constructed dynamically from the region and stack name. Tag all resources using the stack name and meaningful resource names.

We need a CloudFormation template that establishes a baseline set of IAM groups, roles, instance profiles, and managed policies representing common operational personas for an AWS account: a system administrator persona with near-full access outside of IAM itself, an IAM administrator persona with full IAM access, an instance operations persona limited to EC2, Elastic Load Balancing, CloudWatch, and Auto Scaling actions while being explicitly denied the ability to modify VPC networking constructs, a read-only administrator persona covering broad read-only access across core services, and a read-only billing persona limited to viewing billing information. Every EC2-assumable role should have a corresponding instance profile. Every non-billing policy must require that the caller has multi-factor authentication present, must deny access to the AWS Billing console, and must deny the ability to disable, delete, or otherwise tamper with logging-related KMS keys. Output the IDs of each of the created groups.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with a private address range spanning three Availability Zones, laid out as three tiers: a web tier, an application tier, and a database tier, each with one subnet per Availability Zone using distinct CIDR blocks carved out of the VPC's range. Attach an Internet Gateway to the VPC with a single web-tier route table that has a default route to it, shared across all three web subnets. For the application and database tiers, create a NAT Gateway with its own Elastic IP in each web-tier subnet, and give each application and database subnet its own route table with a default route through the NAT Gateway in the corresponding Availability Zone. Expose the VPC ID, the Availability Zones used, and the lists of web, application, and database subnet IDs as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the shared IAM roles and instance profiles required by the Amazon EKS Quick Start stacks in our account, using the prefix "eks-quickstart" for all role names and storing parameter values under the SSM path "/quickstart/amazon-eks". The template should provision Lambda execution roles for various EKS operations including copying zip artifacts from S3, reading resource information (with read-only access across the account in addition to basic Lambda execution permissions), creating the VPC role, deleting bucket contents, cleaning up load balancers, cleaning up security group dependencies, cleaning up Lambda functions, resolving caller ARNs, registering custom resource types, managing node security groups, creating Fargate profiles, and resolving SSM parameters, along with the EKS control plane role that can be assumed by the EKS service, attaches the AWS managed AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and AmazonEKSServicePolicy policies, and additionally allows describing EC2 account attributes, addresses, and internet gateways; the Fargate execution role that can be assumed by the EKS Fargate pods service; and both managed and unmanaged node instance roles with corresponding instance profiles that can be assumed by EC2 instances, attach the AWS managed AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, and AmazonElasticFileSystemReadOnlyAccess policies, and also allow signaling stack completion back to CloudFormation; plus the role creation role that allows Lambda to create the fixed-name IAM role "CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC" and to attach only the AWS managed AWSLambdaENIManagementAccess and AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole policies to that specific role.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a small VPC for a lab environment, with two subnets designated for a web tier and two subnets designated for an application tier, spread across two Availability Zones, all associated with a single shared route table. Create a security group for the web tier that allows inbound HTTPS traffic from within the VPC's own address range. The stack should also create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 that allows read access from any principal, and interface VPC endpoints for Kinesis Data Firehose and Kinesis Data Streams placed in the web-tier subnets and associated with the web security group, so that resources in the VPC can reach these services privately. Expose the VPC ID, all four subnet IDs, and the web security group ID as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that provisions the shared, per-account IAM roles required to support multiple Amazon EKS cluster deployments driven by CloudFormation custom resources backed by Lambda functions in this account, so that these prerequisites only need to be created once rather than per cluster. Create Lambda execution roles for a set of custom-resource handlers responsible for tasks such as copying deployment assets between S3 buckets, reading arbitrary AWS resources, creating a VPC-related IAM role, deleting the contents of S3 buckets, cleaning up orphaned load balancers and their dependent security groups and network interfaces after cluster teardown, cleaning up leftover Lambda functions, looking up the calling identity, registering CloudFormation resource provider types and associated custom resources, resolving Systems Manager parameters under a common configuration path, and creating the IAM role that CloudFormation itself assumes when provisioning cluster VPC resources, each scoped to only the specific AWS actions that task requires. Also create an IAM role for the EKS control plane itself with the standard EKS managed policies, an IAM role that Fargate profiles assume, and both managed-node and unmanaged-node EC2 instance roles, each with a matching instance profile, carrying the standard EKS worker node, CNI, container registry read, and EFS read-only managed policies plus permission to signal CloudFormation on startup. All resource and role names should be derived from a single common name prefix so that they stay consistent across the deployment.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a dedicated IAM user and group for sending email through Amazon SES via SMTP, along with an access key for that user and a policy limiting it to the ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail actions. Since IAM access keys cannot be used directly as SMTP credentials, the stack should include a Lambda-backed custom resource that converts the user's secret access key into a valid SES SMTP password using AWS's published SMTP credential conversion algorithm, and stores both the resulting SMTP username and password as SecureString parameters in Systems Manager Parameter Store under names derived from the IAM username. Provide parameters for the desired IAM username (defaulting to SMTPUser), an access key rotation version number, the Lambda function's log retention period, and an optional ARN of a customer-managed KMS key to encrypt the stored parameters instead of the default AWS-managed key. Include the Lambda function's execution role with permissions to write to Parameter Store, and a CloudWatch Log Group for its execution logs.

We need a CloudFormation template that implements the CloudWatch alarm and CloudTrail logging requirements of Section 3, and Section 2.1 through 2.4, of the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.1.0. The stack should create a dedicated S3 bucket, retained on stack deletion, with a bucket policy allowing CloudTrail to write to it and check its ACL, apply a lifecycle rule that expires objects after 365 days and transitions them to Glacier storage after 90 days in regions that support Glacier, and create a multi-region CloudTrail trail with log file validation enabled that logs to both that S3 bucket and a CloudWatch Logs log group, using a dedicated IAM role that allows CloudTrail to write to the log group. It should also create an SNS topic that emails a specified address, and, for each of fourteen CIS-mandated conditions, a CloudWatch Logs metric filter over the CloudTrail log group paired with a CloudWatch alarm that notifies the SNS topic whenever at least one matching event occurs within a five-minute period; the fourteen conditions to cover are unauthorized API calls, console sign-in without MFA, root account usage, IAM policy changes, CloudTrail configuration changes, console sign-in authentication failures, disabling or scheduling deletion of customer managed KMS keys, S3 bucket policy changes, AWS Config configuration changes, security group changes, network ACL changes, changes to network gateways, route table changes, and VPC changes. The notification email address and the name of the CloudTrail log group should be configurable parameters.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a WebSocket API using API Gateway, backed by a single Python Lambda function that handles the connect, disconnect, default, and a custom message route, intended to push live status updates about grant-processing jobs to connected clients. The Lambda function should have an IAM execution role with basic logging permissions plus a scoped policy allowing it to read and write items in a DynamoDB table used to track connections and to decrypt using KMS, and its environment variables should be encrypted with a dedicated customer-managed KMS key, with key rotation enabled, that only that function and a short list of related functions in this same account are allowed to use for decryption; grant API Gateway permission to invoke the function for every route. Deploy the API to a stage and configure API Gateway account-level CloudWatch logging through a dedicated IAM role, with the underlying CloudWatch Logs log group encrypted using a second, separate customer-managed KMS key created for that purpose. Expose the WebSocket connection URL, the secure WSS endpoint URL, and the API's ARN as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the IAM roles and instance profile needed to support a CodeDeploy and CodePipeline based release pipeline demo. It should include an EC2 instance role and matching instance profile granting broad administrative access for testing purposes, a CodeDeploy service role that can be assumed by the CodeDeploy service in the us-east-1 and us-west-2 regions with permissions to describe EC2 instances and manage Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks for blue/green style deployments, and a CodePipeline service role with the permissions needed to read and write pipeline artifacts in S3 and to orchestrate deployments across Elastic Beanstalk, EC2, Elastic Load Balancing, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch, S3, CloudFormation, RDS, SQS, ECS, CodeDeploy, and Lambda, including the ability to pass IAM roles to those services.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a serverless webhook handler wiring together Stripe payments and our Squarespace Commerce store to post sales notifications to Slack. It should provision an API Gateway REST API with a POST /webhooks endpoint, deployed to a prod stage, backed by a Lambda function that parses an incoming Stripe webhook event, looks up the corresponding Squarespace order and its inventory details, and publishes a formatted notification message to an SNS topic that the stack also creates for relaying to Slack. The template should include the Lambda function's execution role (with permission to publish to that topic), the permission allowing API Gateway to invoke the function, a CloudWatch alarm that triggers whenever the function's invocation errors exceed zero within a one-minute period, and the function's log group. The Squarespace API token and the Stripe webhook signing secret should be accepted as required input parameters so no secrets are hardcoded in the template.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained test environment for an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis replication group with cluster mode enabled, spread across two Availability Zones for resilience testing purposes. It should build its own VPC (defaulting to a 10.0.0.0/22 CIDR block) with two private subnets in different Availability Zones (defaulting to 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24), a security group permitting traffic between those subnets, and an ElastiCache subnet group. The replication group should have Multi-AZ and automatic failover enabled, two shards with one replica each, and both at-rest and in-transit encryption turned on using a customer-managed KMS key that the stack also creates. It should also include an SNS topic, encrypted with that same key, with a policy allowing CloudWatch to publish alarm notifications to it, and an IAM role with a minimal policy allowing it to send SSM Automation signals, to support an automated approval step in a resilience or gameday testing runbook.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS AppSync GraphQL API for a simple songs service, secured with IAM authorization and with request tracing enabled. The GraphQL schema should define a Song type with id, name, and artist fields, a getSongs query returning all songs, and an addSong mutation that accepts a name and artist. Song records should be stored in a DynamoDB table (using id as the partition key) that the template also creates, along with the IAM service role AppSync needs to read from and write to that table. The addSong mutation should be implemented as a two-step pipeline resolver: the first step validates that the submitted artist value contains only letters and returns a validation error if it is missing or invalid, and the second step writes the new song into DynamoDB with an automatically generated id. The DynamoDB table should be retained if the stack is ever deleted or replaced.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito user pool used to authenticate users by email address, enforcing a strong password policy that requires uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and symbol characters with a minimum length of eight, along with an app client (with no client secret) that supports username/password and refresh-token based sign-in. It should also create a regional REST API secured by a Cognito user pool authorizer, exposing a protected GET /me endpoint that only accepts requests carrying a valid access token and returns the caller's authenticated identity claims, plus an unauthenticated GET /open endpoint for comparison that returns the same style of response without requiring a token. Both endpoints should be backed by the same Lambda function, with the appropriate permission granted for API Gateway to invoke it, and deployed to a prod stage.

We need a CloudFormation template that connects our AWS account to the third-party marbot.io monitoring and alerting service. Given our marbot endpoint ID as a parameter, it should set up an EventBridge API destination and connection, authenticated with an API key derived from that endpoint ID, along with a scheduled rule that runs every 30 days to post our account and stack identification details to marbot's service in order to establish and keep the connection alive, plus the IAM role EventBridge needs to invoke that destination. The template should also create a cross-account IAM role that marbot's AWS account can assume, using an external ID unique to this stack, to perform monitoring on our behalf, with permissions gated behind separate boolean feature flags for automatically configuring CloudWatch alarms and monitoring rules across our resources, enriching account IDs with friendly aliases, embedding metric graphs into CloudWatch alarm notifications, and approving or rejecting CodePipeline manual approval requests. When the automatic monitoring feature is enabled, that role's own permissions to manage its resources should additionally be restricted by an IAM permissions boundary policy created by the stack. Finally, the template should register the account connection with marbot's service using a custom resource.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained backend for a simple mobile or web application. It should provision a DynamoDB table with a numeric id as the partition key, provisioned for 10 read and 10 write capacity units, plus a global secondary index also keyed on id with 5 read and 10 write capacity units. It should also create a Cognito identity pool that allows unauthenticated guest access, along with the IAM role assumed by unauthenticated identities and the identity pool role attachment linking the two. That unauthenticated role should be granted permission to submit mobile analytics events, use Cognito Sync, publish to SNS topics, and write items into DynamoDB, so guest users of the app can interact with these services directly from the client.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Glue Data Catalog database along with an optional crawler and an optional Spark ETL job, forming the catalog and transform layer of a data lake. It should accept a naming prefix and an environment (dev, staging, or prod) used to build the database, crawler, and job names, along with the ARN and prefix of an existing S3 bucket that the crawler scans for schema and partition discovery. The crawler should run on a configurable cron schedule (defaulting to once daily), only log rather than automatically apply schema and partition changes it detects, only scan newly added data on each run, and be toggleable on or off through a parameter (off changes nothing about the catalog itself). The ETL job, also toggleable and off by default, should be a Glue Spark job with a configurable worker type, worker count, timeout, and maximum concurrent runs, reading its script from an S3 location supplied as a parameter, writing transformed output under a separate target S3 bucket and prefix, using job bookmarks so reruns only process new data, and logging continuously to a CloudWatch log group with a configurable retention period. Both the crawler and the job should share one IAM service role scoped to read access on the source bucket and, when a target bucket is supplied, write access on that target bucket as well.
